claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked over a field (the integer graph windows are tensored with Q, so Q1, dim Q1 and dim H1 are Q-quantities): d1 descends to Q1 = C1/im d0 exactly when d1 o d0 = 0 (an instance with d1 d0 != 0 has no kappa1 and two representatives of the zero class with different d1 values); H1 = ker kappa1 is the image of ker d1 in Q1 and a class is closed iff every representative is. For the abstract defect IsPhi (attained minimum of a function J over h + im d0): it is repair invariant and unique; for nonnegative definite J it is nonnegative and zero exactly on the zero class. BRIDGE (kernel): for the weighted-L1 graph cost, cost D w h x = wl1 w (h + negD D x), IsPhi (wl1 w) (negD D) is the attained minimum of cost (isPhi_graph_iff), wl1 is nonnegative and, for positive weights, definite, so Phi1 = 0 iff the class is zero for EVERY graph window with positive weights (graph_phi_zero_iff). Weak duality and its certificate form isPhi_of_certificate (a primal potential x and a dual vector y with equal values give the attained minimum); the filled triangle has Phi1 = Gamma2 = 2. Every (Phi1, Gamma2) pair lies in exactly one of ExactClass / ClosedResidual / ActiveClosureFailure; for Phi1 >= 0 the spellings phi != 0 and phi > 0 agree (ne_zero_iff_pos). Native table over 17 graph windows (loop, disconnected, empty C2, d1 = 0, zero class, weights, a gauge-shifted pair, two windows with d1 d0 != 0 marked NotAWindow with a kappa witness): every record carries a primal potential x and a dual vector y that the checker verifies exactly (cost(x) = y.h = Phi1, d0^T y = 0, |y_e| <= w_e), plus the dual-LP value recomputed independently of the producer; the two gauge-shifted windows must carry equal Phi1, Gamma2, R_cl and class. For a non-window Phi1 (a class function of d0, J, h) is kept and Gamma2 is withheld, because the representative norm ||d1 h||_1 depends on the representative there.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any derivation of the window from Genesis admission or Real_0 (it stays a declared datum); norms other than weighted L1; non-graph d0 beyond the module-level lemmas; existence of the attained minimum for the weighted-L1 cost as a Lean theorem (attainment is part of IsPhi and is witnessed natively by x and y, but LP strong duality / minimiser existence is not formalised); complex coefficients; any meaning of Gamma2 for a non-window (representative dependent); that R_cl = Gamma2/Phi1 mixes the weighted Phi1 with the unweighted Gamma2 and so depends on the weight scale; any physical reading of the three classes.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For modules over a field (the graph windows tensored with Q), kappa1 exists on Q1 = C1/im d0 exactly when d1 d0 = 0 (kernel); for graph windows with positive weights the weighted-L1 cost is the IsPhi defect of a nonnegative definite J, so Phi1 = 0 iff the class is zero (kernel); on the 17 tabulated integer windows Phi1 is the weighted-L1 minimum over rational potentials with a verified primal potential and dual vector; each (Phi1, Gamma2) pair has exactly one class: ExactClass iff Phi1 = 0, ClosedResidual iff Phi1 > 0 and Gamma2 = 0, ActiveClosureFailure iff both are positive (the Lean diag theorems state phi != 0, equivalent for Phi1 >= 0).
claim_boundary.next_test: Prove in Lean that the weighted-L1 quotient defect of every graph window is attained (existence of a minimising potential, or strong duality for the pair of linear programs), so that the attainment clause of IsPhi becomes a theorem for the windows instead of resting on the verified primal and dual witnesses tabulated here.
